chapter: Blanton, Los Angeles and Art Tatum
title: What Tatum admired: Garner, Fats Waller and Don Lambert
summary: Tatum talked about Garner, Fats Waller and especially the Princeton pianist Don Lambert, whom he loved.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: Did you ever talk with Tatum about the be-boppers? Did he ever talk to you about -- did you ever ask him what he thought about it?
No, we never talked to him hardly at all about it. We were so wrapped up in what we were doing together, you know.
Who were some of the -- did Tatum talk much about any of the musicians that he did like -- did you -- some of the people you know he liked.
Whom he liked, oh, yes. He talked -- he talked about Erroll Garner and --
I know he liked Fats Waller.

Fats, oh, yes. Yes. There were a couple of -- oh, a couple of other idols. Another one of his idols, you didn't hear very much about him --a pianist then was from Princeton, New Jersey. His name was Donald -- Don Lambert.
And he was -- Tatum loved him.
Tatum used to tell us about how much piano Don used to play, and he used to really play a whole lot of piano, you know. Tatum loved him.
Did you get a chance to hear Lambert yourself?
I think I heard him a couple of times, yes. Yes.
